title: Atoms: The Tiny Builders
summary: Everything is made of atoms. See what is inside one, and what elements are.

steps.title: Smaller than small
sentences: All matter is made of tiny particles called atoms.
A single atom is so small that several hundred thousand of them would fit across the width of a human hair.
Atoms join together to make everything, from air to your body.

steps.title: Inside an atom
sentences: At the centre of an atom is the nucleus, made of protons and neutrons.
Protons have a positive charge, and neutrons have no charge.
Tiny electrons with a negative charge move around the nucleus.

steps.title: Elements
sentences: An element is a substance made of only one kind of atom, such as hydrogen, oxygen, iron or gold.
The number of protons decides which element an atom is.
The periodic table arranges all the known elements, and there are 118 of them.

steps.title: Molecules
sentences: Atoms can join to form molecules.
Two hydrogen atoms and one oxygen atom make one molecule of water, H2O.
Changing how atoms join is what happens in a chemical reaction.

facts: Most of an atom is empty space.
The periodic table was first organised by Dmitri Mendeleev in 1869.
About ninety percent of the atoms in the Universe are hydrogen.

quiz.q: What is at the centre of an atom?
quiz.why: The nucleus is at the centre.

quiz.q: Which particle has a negative charge?

options: Two hydrogen atoms and one oxygen atom
quiz.why: The formula H2O means two hydrogen and one oxygen.

notes: 118 is the number of elements confirmed at the time of writing; a new element would be a major discovery.
